recordings.title: Natural reflection on audience growth and the day
recordings.topic: Disfluent personal narrative, reciprocal action, quantity change, contrast, and emotion
recordings.transcript: Today was an interesting day in the aspects of InPublic. I really understood what I was doing for once on the I was trying to grow an audience and I was doing the follow back follow method where we was gonna follow each other, where I had to follow people, and I had to just follow them back at the same time. But one of the main things I was encountering I was encountering the x time I was with I was being timed out ever so often, and people were like, follow me back, bro. Follow me back, bro. And it was really interesting. It was the first time I really grew from 60 followers to about 400 and something. And was one of the most times I actually enjoyed when I was grinding in that sense. But I today also today, I challenged someone and I was like, I didn't know you were willing to add me the best for the win, and I was kinda shocked because I didn't know he was just it's our prototype, bro. And I was like, he surrendering. In my head, I was like, he surrender. One time, I was like, no. I'm embarrassed. Like, he was so weak. I was like, was going to my mind, but I didn't really say that, but that's what I was thinking. But that's just what happened today. Today was a really nice day. Compared to yesterday, today was a much better day. I I accomplished a lot, and I'm moving forward.

recordings.title: Natural explanation of InPublic
recordings.topic: Abstract system explanation, data flow, relationships, spatial language, and aspiration
recordings.transcript: Speaker. This is InPublic. Speaking normally. Deepgram is listening to what I'm saying, and from that speech, InPublic starts deciding what actually deserves being shown visually. Then it sends ideas into Excalidraw. Text boxes, relationships, arrows, structures, while I'm still talking, the interesting part isn't the transcript. I don't want just subtitles on the speech. I want the canvas to actually express what I mean. So if I explain an idea, the structure of the idea starts the structure of the idea should start appearing besides me and Rita. There's still a lot I want to include, especially how expressive the videos can be. Because this is where InPublic is right now.

recordings.title: Recorded business explanation
recordings.topic: Revenue/churn change, causal attribution, and priorities
recordings.transcript: Our revenue increased after we launched the new plan, but churn increased too. Most of that churn came from new customers who cancelled after their first month. So our next priority is improving onboarding and retention.

recordings.title: Recorded photosynthesis lesson
recordings.topic: Concrete objects, inputs, directed creation, release, and process
recordings.transcript: Photosynthesis starts when a plant absorbs sunlight. The plant takes carbon dioxide from the air, and water from the soil. It uses that energy to create glucose, and releases oxygen.

recordings.title: Recorded launch plan
recordings.topic: Ordered dependencies, priorities, quantities, and actions
recordings.transcript: Before we launch, we need to finish payments first. Then optimize latency and usage costs. After that, bring in ten testers, collect their feedback, and prepare the public launch.

recordings.title: Focused sequence fixture
recordings.transcript: First, we collect the data. Then we clean the data. Finally, we train the model. Once that's finished, I can explain the result to the team.

recordings.title: Focused cause/effect fixture
recordings.topic: Causal chain followed by explicitly uncertain correlation
recordings.transcript: Marketing creates traffic. And that traffic creates more sign ups. That gives the team a useful way to explain what happened. After we changed the website, sign ups increased, but I don't know if one caused the other. We will keep measuring before we make a stronger claim.

recordings.title: Focused comparison fixture
recordings.topic: Two-sided option comparison and unresolved choice
recordings.transcript: Option A is cheaper and faster to set up. Option B costs more. But it gives you more control. I'm still deciding which one I would actually choose.
